exercises.video_explanation_script: Start by positioning yourself with your upper back against a bench, barbell across your hips. Your feet should be flat and positioned so that when you're at the top, your shins are vertical. From here, drive through your heels and squeeze your glutes to push your hips up. At the top, your body should form a straight line from shoulders to knees - this is where you really squeeze those glutes hard. Avoid arching your lower back; instead, think about tucking your tailbone slightly. Lower back down with control and repeat. The magic happens when you feel this entirely in your glutes, not your lower back.

exercises.video_explanation_script: The RDL is all about the hip hinge. Start standing tall with the bar at your hips. From here, push your hips back like you're trying to close a car door behind you. Keep your spine neutral and the bar close to your legs as you lower down. You should feel a deep stretch in your hamstrings. Only go as low as you can while keeping your back flat. Then drive your hips forward to stand back up, squeezing your glutes at the top. This isn't a squat - your knees stay at roughly the same angle the whole time. The movement comes from your hips.

exercises.video_explanation_script: The Bulgarian split squat is one of the best exercises for building strong, powerful glutes. Set up with your rear foot elevated on a bench behind you and your front foot planted firmly 2-3 feet in front. From here, lower down by bending your front knee and dropping your rear knee toward the ground. Think of this as a single-leg squat - your back leg is just there for balance. Keep your torso upright and make sure you're driving through that front heel. At the bottom, you should feel a great stretch in your glute and hip flexor. Then drive back up through your front heel, squeezing your glute at the top. All the work should be coming from that front leg.

exercises.video_explanation_script: The glute bridge is a foundational movement for building strong glutes. Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor, positioned close to your glutes. From here, drive through your heels and squeeze your glutes to lift your hips off the floor. At the top, your body should form a straight line from your shoulders to your knees. Really focus on that glute squeeze at the top - that's where the magic happens. Avoid arching your lower back; instead, think about tucking your tailbone slightly. Lower back down with control and repeat. This exercise is perfect for learning how to engage your glutes and is great for activation before heavier lifts.

exercises.video_explanation_script: The cable pull-through is fantastic for learning the hip hinge and building powerful glutes. Set the cable at the lowest setting with a rope attachment. Stand facing away from the machine and reach between your legs to grab the rope. Walk forward until you feel tension. From here, push your hips back, letting the weight pull you into a hinge position. You should feel a stretch in your hamstrings and glutes. Then explosively drive your hips forward, pulling the cable through, and squeeze your glutes hard at the top. Your arms are just holding the rope - all the power comes from your hips. This is a great teaching tool for the hip hinge pattern.

exercises.video_explanation_script: Step-ups are an incredibly functional exercise for building strong glutes and legs. Stand facing a box with one foot fully planted on top - make sure your whole foot is on there, not just your toes. From here, drive through the heel of your elevated foot to step up onto the box. The key is to not push off with your bottom foot - that leg is just along for the ride. All the work should come from the leg on the box. Stand tall at the top and squeeze your glute. Then control your descent back down. The higher the box, the more you'll emphasize your glutes. This exercise is fantastic for addressing imbalances between legs.

exercises.video_explanation_script: The curtsy lunge is excellent for targeting your glutes, especially the gluteus medius on the side of your hip. Start standing with feet hip-width apart. Step one leg back and across behind your front leg, like you're doing a curtsy. Lower down until your back knee is just above the ground and your front thigh is close to parallel. The key here is to keep your hips square - don't let them rotate. You should feel a great stretch on the outside of your front glute. Push through your front heel to return to standing, squeezing your glute at the top. This exercise challenges your balance and stability while building strong, shapely glutes.

exercises.video_explanation_script: The single-leg RDL is one of the most challenging and rewarding exercises for your glutes, hamstrings, and balance. Stand on one leg with a slight bend in your knee. From here, push your hips back as you hinge forward, extending your free leg behind you. Think of your torso and back leg as one unit - they move together. Keep your hips square to the ground; don't let them open up. Lower down until your torso is about parallel to the ground, feeling a deep stretch in your glute and hamstring. Then drive through your heel to return to standing, squeezing your glute at the top. This exercise is as much about control and stability as it is about strength.

exercises.video_explanation_script: The sumo deadlift is a powerful variation that emphasizes your glutes, inner thighs, and quads. Set up with a wide stance - feet well outside shoulder-width - with your toes pointed out. Hinge down to grip the bar with your hands inside your knees. From here, push your knees out, keep your chest up, and drive through the entire foot to stand up. The bar should travel straight up, close to your body. Think about pushing the floor away rather than pulling the bar up. At the top, squeeze your glutes hard and stand tall. The wider stance allows for a more upright torso and puts more emphasis on your glutes compared to conventional deadlifts.

exercises.video_explanation_script: Banded lateral walks are one of the best exercises for targeting your glute medius - the muscle on the side of your hip that's crucial for stability. Place a resistance band around your legs - above your knees for easier, around your ankles for harder. Get into an athletic quarter-squat position and create tension in the band. From here, take controlled steps to the side, maintaining that low position the entire time. The key is to keep your knees pushed out against the band - never let them cave inward. You should feel this burning on the outside of your hips. This exercise is perfect for warming up before leg day or as a finisher to really torch those glutes.

exercises.video_explanation_script: Frog pumps are an incredible exercise for building that mind-muscle connection with your glutes and achieving an amazing pump. Lie on your back and bring the soles of your feet together, pulling them close to your glutes. Let your knees drop out to the sides - you'll look like a frog, hence the name. From here, drive through the outer edges of your feet and squeeze your glutes to lift your hips off the ground. At the top, really focus on that squeeze - hold it for a second or two. Lower back down and repeat. The frog-leg position puts your glutes in a shortened position, allowing for maximum contraction. This is perfect for high reps at the end of your workout to really finish off those glutes.

exercises.video_explanation_script: The deficit reverse lunge is an advanced variation that takes the regular reverse lunge to the next level. Stand on an elevated platform - 2 to 4 inches high. From here, step one leg back off the platform and lower your back knee toward the ground. The elevation allows you to get a much deeper range of motion and a better stretch in your front glute. Keep your torso upright and your front shin relatively vertical. Then drive through your front heel to return to standing on the platform, squeezing your glute at the top. This increased range of motion makes the deficit reverse lunge one of the best exercises for building powerful glutes.
